_meta.purpose: Coordinates for the place strings used in Cronologia chronology datasets. The site build is network-free (core ADR-0004), so coordinates cannot be looked up at build time; they are committed here instead.
_meta.usage: A place string may name MORE THAN ONE location and therefore resolves to a LIST of ids. Resolve with tools/places.py, never by splitting strings ad hoc.
_meta.coordinateSource: OpenStreetMap Nominatim, ODbL 1.0 (https://osm.org/copyright). Every entry records the exact display_name it was confirmed against, so a wrong match is auditable rather than invisible.
_meta.curation: Candidates were PROPOSED by tools/places.py --propose and accepted only after reading the returned display_name. Top hits were wrong in several cases: "Astana" returned a castle in Malaysia, "Cairo" returned Cairo, Illinois, "Fribourg" returned the canton rather than the city where the SSPX was founded, "Lucca" returned the province rather than the city, and "Bloomington (Monroe County), Indiana, USA" returned a filling station. Nothing here was auto-accepted.
_meta.precision: settlement = a town/city/hamlet centre. country-centroid = a whole country or region; the point is NOT where anything happened and must be rendered differently from a settlement, or omitted from maps.
_meta.nonGeographic: Entries with kind "non-geographic" resolve deliberately to NO coordinates. "Worldwide", "international" and survey populations are scopes, not places; dropping a pin for them would invent a location the source does not claim.
_meta.jurisdictions: Some place strings name ecclesiastical jurisdictions (e.g. "Diocese of Arlington"). These are pinned at the see city with a note; the pin marks the see, never the territory.
